scope: Experimental scalable SQL reads guarded at execution by an actual audited native owner. Strict query entry points retain full retained-carrier and entity-history checks.

limitations: The owned entry points require a matching companion and successful full retained audit activation. Enrollment-only arm cannot satisfy the execution guard.
The host must keep enrolled handles private, submit standalone activation, and invalidate before raw or legacy dispatch. The native observer does not prevent arbitrary SQL on an enrolled handle.
No fast native-write maintenance is included. A host invalidation requires full revalidation before subsequent owned reads.
The only planner difference is the integrity CTE and explicit owned reason prefix. DISTINCT, typed value semantics, temporal cuts, and logical input/intermediate/output gates are retained.
Logical query budgets do not guarantee a physical DuckDB allocator or process-memory ceiling.
These are functional parity and invalidation tests. No performance adoption claim has been measured in this slice.
The worker uses copied integration build metadata version 0.19.0. The integrating branch must rebuild its core and then the companion so their pinned hashes agree.

review.result: No blocker after checking shared control/attachment/FP guard retention, volatile validated ownership, unchanged planner bounds, and explicit owned reasons. Trusted-dispatch contract remains required.
